White-Label — One Card Platform, Two Relationships

"Northstar — an online brokerage offering an Arta-powered, portfolio-secured card to eligible investors." The product sits inside Northstar's own app shell: Northstar owns discovery, navigation, brand and the customer relationship; Arta powers eligibility, decisioning, compliance, security and AI guardrails.

The visual language adapts; the decision integrity stays consistent.

Platform ownership model

LayerArta controlsPartner configures / owns
DistributionCard capability & eligibility APIApp shell, entry point, promotion
ProductEligible-asset & limit logicProduct name, benefits, card artwork
ApplicationRequired data & decision statesTheme, tone, supporting content
ComplianceMandatory disclosures & consentJurisdiction-approved brand wording
SecurityAuthentication & fraud standardsPartner login entry, account shell
AIData permissions, explanation, confirmation, escalationAssistant name, visual identity, notification tone
ServicingCard status, payment & dispute capabilitiesNavigation, support-handoff presentation

What partners cannot change

  • Hide or de-emphasise fees, or reduce the prominence of critical warnings with brand styling
  • Remove the portfolio / market-movement risk explanation
  • Alter a decisioning outcome — or present pending as approved
  • Remove the next step from a decline or adjusted offer
  • Pre-check any consent
  • Let the AI move money or sell assets without explicit confirmation
  • Hide which data the AI used

In implementation: theme tokens, content schemas, protected components and partner-level configuration permissions — the token pipeline already rejects governance violations at build time.
